newsitem.title: ITALY: TIM seeks authority to offer cordless phone.
newsitem.headline: TIM seeks authority to offer cordless phone.

text.p: Italy's mobile phone group Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) has asked the Italian Post Ministry for authorisation to offer a cordless phone service, said the group's managing director Vito Gamberale.
Gamberale was speaking to reporters at an annual mobile communication meeting, Mobicom 96.
TIM's sister company Telecom Italia announced plans in October to launch an advanced cordless phone using the Digital European Cordless Telephony (DECT) standard.

But this immediately ran into controversary when anti-trust chairman Giuliano Amato said that if it went ahead it would be taking advantage of its dominant position in the fixed line market and compete head-on with mobile phone companies.
Both TIM and Telecom Italia are majority-owned by state-controlled telecoms holding company STET.
Gamberale said, "The group is putting together its own strategy based on its available means.

"Seen that the market has shown that other mobile operators in Italy are heading towards this service, we have presented a demand to the ministry for authorisation with our majority shareholder STET," he said.
Asked how TIM would launch this initiative in respect to Telecom Italia he limited his comments to, "Certainly, even Telecom Italia is committing itself in this direction".
At 1445 GMT, TIM shares were up 0.58 percent at 3,620 lire, Telecom Italia was off 1.33 percent at 3,555 lire and STET was down 1.18 percent at 6,460 lire in an overall lower Milan market.
